h: Windmills, woods and the Essex coast
p: Rayleigh is a handy base for an active day because so much of south Essex is within a short hop. Start with a trampoline session while the kids are buzzing, then spend the rest of the day outdoors, or flip it round if the forecast says the afternoon will be the soggy bit. Either way, an hour or so of bouncing plus kit-up time slots neatly into a morning or after lunch.

Right next to Rayleigh Mount stands the town's windmill, a striking landmark you can't miss as you come into the centre. A little further out, Hockley Woods is a large spread of ancient woodland with marked trails and a play area, so it's perfect for a calmer second act. If you want proper views, Hadleigh Country Park looks out over the Thames Estuary and was the venue for the mountain biking at the London 2012 Olympics. The crumbling towers of Hadleigh Castle sit on the slope nearby and make a dramatic backdrop for photos.

Heading to Southend afterwards? The pier stretches way out into the estuary and has its own little train, and Adventure Island sits by the seafront for rides and arcade fun. Rayleigh station is on the line into London Liverpool Street, so visiting without a car is doable too. Pack a spare top for each child, because a sweaty trampolinist plus an estuary breeze is not a winning combination.
